assessment.intent: Help a business owner decide when paying ongoing maintenance for a custom AI workflow is justified, and when a general tool is enough.
assessment.specificity: The article stays focused on one decision, uses a practical worksheet, a clearly hypothetical worked example and specific pre-commitment questions rather than drifting into general AI advice.
assessment.evidence: The advice is grounded in a visible decision framework and Michael's stated AI audit and custom-system scope, without inventing client results, tests or percentages.
assessment.voice: The voice is direct, practical and owner-aware: it explains workflow, integration and fallback in plain language, and it treats custom AI as business infrastructure rather than magic.
assessment.usefulAsset: This is a strong buying-stage article because it gives an owner a way to compare the cost of a recurring business problem against the full cost of owning and maintaining a custom workflow.
